comms-digest.summary: Scheduled Google Chat and Gmail digest that surfaces only what needs one person, proposes numbered email and Chat clean-up, and runs a weekly reversible sidebar tidy. Use for a twice-daily comms digest, a Monday sidebar tidy, or restoring a sidebar from a snapshot. Never sends, posts, replies, marks read, or permanently deletes. Do not use for interactive triage or sending replies.

engos-audit-change-impact.summary: Roll up an org's merged and open GitLab and GitHub changes for a time window into a fact-checked, business-impact report: each bullet states its likely impact (inference) and what changed (fact) with links. The roster is the reporting tree in the Appian Home org chart. Use for what-did-my-org-ship-and-why-it-matters updates; do not use for git metrics dashboards, Jira or chat status reports, or code review.

engos-audit-code-health.summary: Perform a read-only structural audit of a brownfield codebase, measuring hotspots, coupling, god objects, dead-code candidates, prior findings, and drift. Use for repository health; do not use for feature completeness or diff review.

engos-audit-engineering-progress.summary: Generate a Git-derived engineering progress dashboard for one repository or a configured fleet, including activity, churn, authors, and releases. Use for periodic engineering activity audits; do not use for Jira story points, feature completeness, code review, or code-quality approval.

engos-audit-feature-status.summary: Audit a feature’s stated scope against code, tests, configuration, specifications, tickets, and Git history, then report completion states, drift, gaps, and shipping priorities. Use for feature readiness; do not use for repository-wide health or Git-only activity reports.

engos-audit-opex-incident-review.summary: Generate an evidence-backed Daily OpEx Digest and optional incident drill-downs from current Jira incidents, prior snapshots, DPAs, and postmortems. Use for decisions, owner accountability, daily progress, stalled work, estate patterns, SLA tracking, Five Whys, and executive meeting preparation.

engos-audit-pitch-review.summary: Create, review, score, improve, or export Shape Up pitches by checking problem framing, appetite, architecture, rendered diagram and contract artifacts, dependencies, integration proof, risks, and betting readiness. Use for pitch artifacts; do not use for feature status or general proposal synthesis.

engos-audit-weekly-intel.summary: Collect and fact-check project information from issue trackers, Git, code review, Chat, and documents, then produce one executive report with technical appendices and source confidence. Use for multi-source periodic intelligence; do not use for Git-only reports, inbox triage, or feature audits.

engos-browser-demo-recorder.summary: Plan and generate a complete Playwright browser walkthrough with authentication, realistic pacing, and video capture. Use when the goal is a shareable product demo; do not use for test coverage or CI.

engos-content-dynamic-html-presentations.summary: Create a self-contained HTML presentation and, when requested, validated PNG or image-only PPTX exports from a topic, outline, or source material. Use for visual narrative deliverables; do not use for browser demos or plain reports.

engos-debug-diagnose-failure.summary: Reproduce, localize and explain a software failure using bounded experiments that distinguish competing causes. Use for failing tests, builds or unexpected runtime behavior; return a supported cause or an explicit unknown with evidence for repair handoff.

engos-delivery-address-code-review.summary: Apply selected pull request or merge request feedback with tightly scoped edits, then prepare the fix for re-review. Use only when actionable reviewer comments already exist; use code review for pre-commit or pre-push judgment.

engos-delivery-artifact-embed.summary: Format Framed or Shaped documents and place authored shaping bundles through explicit HTML, PR/MR, chat, Google Doc or wiki adapters. Use native Mermaid or source-bound SVG/PNG, preserve native tables and report unverified placement explicitly.

engos-delivery-diagram-contract-artifact.summary: Author a surface-agnostic shaped-pitch artifact bundle with Mermaid component, sequence, and data-flow diagrams plus API/contracts and security-owner tables. Use when a shaped solution needs durable visual and contract evidence before review or betting; do not invent component internals or place artifacts on external surfaces.

engos-delivery-implement-slice.summary: Implement one bounded software change from an accepted task or clear request, preserve unrelated work, and report verification tied to the actual patch. Use for a scoped feature or repair; use the review-feedback capability when selected reviewer comments define the work.

engos-delivery-resolve-conflict.summary: Analyze and plan the safe resolution of Git or document conflicts while preserving valuable content, exposing contradictions, and defining verification. Use when an actual merge or content conflict exists; do not use for ordinary proposal disagreement without conflict markers.

engos-design-architecture.summary: Design APIs, data models, patterns, or systems with explicit boundaries, trade-offs, failure modes, migration, rollback, and validation. Use for concrete architecture decisions; do not use for prompt hardening or behavioral evaluation.

engos-design-frame-from-vague.summary: Normalize rough input and draft a solution-free frame with affected people, outcome, why-now, actual appetite, walk-away and answerable uncertainties. Supports the shaping conductor; does not choose architecture or invent human decisions.

engos-design-freshness-sweep.summary: Execute a read-only freshness sweep before designing, planning or resuming ticket-backed work. Read every linked-ticket comment and MR note and fourteen days of area-owner merges across involved repos; report changed assumptions and today's simpler path, and refuse technical blocked verdicts without the responsible owner's exact confirmation.

engos-design-plan-implementation.summary: Plan independently verifiable implementation tasks from accepted requirements and an optional supplied design. Use for multi-step planning or revising unfinished work with explicit dependencies, interfaces, allowed writes and stop conditions; preserve the existing tracker and leave execution, delegation and goal creation to their owners.

engos-design-plan-to-goal.summary: Compile a reviewed plan or intent into a host-aware goal, durable specification, and task-specific verifier with explicit trust, drift, stop, and rollback conditions. Use when a bounded long-running goal packet is needed; do not use for ordinary one-step implementation.

engos-design-shaping.summary: Guide product and engineering from rough notes through solution-free framing, evidence collection, shaping, independent review and verified delivery. Use for a shaping workshop, run progress or resume; use pitch review alone for a finished pitch assessment.

engos-design-specify-change.summary: Specify a feature, design-led change, or bugfix with source-backed requirements, acceptance conditions, explicit assumptions and unchanged behavior. Use before planning when the change needs a specification; preserve existing formats and leave architecture, task planning and implementation to their owners.

engos-memory-context-continuity.summary: Maintain durable context, todo, and insight state for a multi-file or multi-source investigation that must survive compaction, session changes, branch changes, or worktree removal. Use when analysis must be resumed; do not use for a one-off report or final decision.

engos-memory-threader.summary: Export the current conversation as a faithful transcript or durable handoff, preserving turn order, AI output fidelity, artifacts, and missing-history disclosure. Use for archival or transfer; do not blend export with analysis.

engos-meta-instruction-editor.summary: Audit, rewrite, diff, or verify prompts, skills, and agent instructions for clarity while preserving commands, authority, safety boundaries, and behavior. Use when instruction preservation is the central task; do not use for general prose editing.

engos-meta-supercharge.summary: Harden a prompt, plan, proposal, or workflow through the smallest useful sequence of simplification, inversion, adversarial critique, contract checks, debate, or grading. Supports `/catchup` for verified session reconstruction with exact tables, status markers, and validation. Use when the artifact needs stronger reasoning or execution guidance; use behavioral evaluation for proof.

engos-meta-uac-import.summary: Improve skills and agents through Core-Prompts plan, judge, and apply while preserving their surface scope. New agent surfaces require explicit user approval. Use for capability intake and improvement; do not use for ordinary prose editing or deployment.

engos-operations-daily-update.summary: Daily update kit for an org's shared status doc in Google Docs. Creates the doc if it does not exist (areas and initiatives, each with an owner), otherwise adds today's updates: each designated leader (the tab's updater) drafts daily updates for their initiatives (or, when they ask, for someone else's) from Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Drive, Jira, GitLab and GitHub, reviews them, and publishes on their OK; the doc owner closes out the day at 3pm (marks missed tabs, rebuilds the overview) and can send a summary to readers. Use when the user types /engos-operations-daily-update (with or without a command such as help, update, close, initiative done, reader add), or says 'do my daily update', 'set up the status doc', or 'close out the day'. Prefer this over daily-status-brief in this folder.

engos-operations-gtd-planning.summary: Run the GTD loop (capture, clarify, organize, reflect, engage) for one person using whatever task system and sources they have. Use when the user says "plan my day", "weekly review", "triage my inbox", "daily close", "plan my week", "capture my tasks", or asks to turn email, chat, comments, calendar or meeting notes into a clean task list. Do not use to manage a team, assign work to others, or edit another person's task system.

engos-operations-gtd-sources.summary: Read-only source adapters that feed the GTD planning method: Gmail, Chat, Drive comments, Calendar and Gemini meeting notes, plus the contract for adding more. Use when the GTD method runs capture or needs calendar and meeting context, or when someone is writing a new source adapter. Do not use to send, reply, post, mark read, accept or edit anything, and do not use without the method skill.

engos-operations-gtd-things3.summary: Task-system adapter that lets the GTD planning method read and write Things 3 on macOS through a bundled script. Use when the profile lists `things3` under adapters, or when the GTD method needs snapshot, inspect, history, capture, relocate, schedule, annotate or retag against Things 3. Do not use on other platforms, for Things Cloud or iOS, or to run the planning method itself.

engos-operations-ic-assistant.summary: Guide an Incident Commander through phase tracking, status cadence, artifact checks, escalation prompts, handoff, resolution, and postmortem work without making incident decisions. Use during an active incident or postmortem.

engos-optimization-auto-research.summary: Run bounded, baseline-controlled experiments to improve prompts, skills, workflows, tools, or code and decide whether a candidate is ready for promotion. Use when better behavior must be measured; do not use for unmeasured brainstorming.

engos-orchestration-batman.summary: Run the explicitly requested, evidence-gated delivery protocol through independent subagents, TDD, blocking reviews, verification, documentation, Git health, and authorized landing. Use for implementation work that requires controller-owned sequencing and evidence.

engos-orchestration-crew.summary: Design, launch and oversee a multi-agent crew in any agent harness (Claude Code, Kiro, Codex, Gemini CLI, or any harness that can start sub-agents and read and write files) that runs a long job to a defined goal against acceptance criteria fixed up front: a lead, workers, fresh verifiers, a safety watch and an independent drift auditor, with change control. Use when the user types /engos-orchestration-crew (with or without a command such as help, design, launch, status, end) or wants a long, checkable, multi-agent job (an A/B evaluation, QA of a built system, an audit or a migration) run unattended with no drift. Do not use for short or single-agent tasks.

engos-quality-code-review.summary: Review a staged change, diff, commit, or branch for correctness, scope, simplicity, lifecycle risk, and merge readiness before commit, push, merge, or release. Use for judgment; do not use to apply reviewer feedback.

engos-quality-docs-review.summary: Review repository documentation for information architecture, stale commands, broken links, misplaced content, drift, and release hygiene. Use when docs quality or discoverability is the primary concern; do not use for ordinary sentence editing.

engos-quality-gitops-review.summary: Assess repository hygiene, commit and pull request or merge request readiness, CI, packaging, merge, tag, and release prerequisites across GitHub and GitLab. Use for release or merge gates; do not claim hosted state without current verification.

engos-quality-shaping-gate.summary: Check whether a shaping stage may advance from its actual artifacts, evidence and prior receipts. Reject solution-in-framing, invented evidence, unresolved material questions, stale reviews and incomplete publication. Use within guided shaping or independent pitch review.

engos-quality-testing-review.summary: Design or generate tests, edge cases, and coverage-gap analysis for a defined behavior without claiming tests were run. Use when test design is the primary deliverable; use GitOps review for release readiness.

engos-reconciliation-converge.summary: Compare multiple sources, drafts, or proposals, surface conflicts and gaps, and produce one defensible recommendation with explicit trade-offs. Use when competing inputs must converge; do not hide incompatible ideas in a blended summary.

engos-route-intent.summary: Choose a starting skill when the desired outcome, next step or needed depth is unclear. Route across the current Core-Prompts catalog, ask material questions with Other/free text, and explain conditional handoffs. Skip intake for clear direct tasks or a named skill.

engos-triage-my-inbox-chat-pulse.summary: Triage Gmail and Google Chat into a deterministic attention queue with priority, links, and approved follow-up actions. Use when deciding what communications need attention; triage is read-only and actions require explicit approval.

jira-intake-review.summary: Daily read-only review of the new tickets in a Jira filter: what came in, what came in sideways (no epic, no initiative, no feature card, wrong home), who owns the fix, and the next action. Use for a weekday morning intake report or an owner-by-owner follow-up draft. Never edits, comments on, assigns, or closes tickets and never sends messages. Do not use for sprint reporting or ticket hygiene sweeps.

loopy.summary: Discover, find, compare, audit, repair, adapt, craft, run, debrief, and prepare repeatable AI-agent loops for publication. Use when a user asks to analyze code or coding threads for recurring work, find a published loop, interview them to turn a goal into a bounded loop, review a loop for weak checks or unsafe authority, execute a loop with an evidence receipt, learn from completed runs, or validate and submit a loop to Loop Library.

relationships.when: Feature behavior or acceptance is unclear.
relationships.handoff: A solution-free frame with affected people, desired outcome, actual appetite and open questions. After the owner accepts the frame, specify a concrete change if acceptance needs definition, or choose a full shaping workshop if requested.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: Accepted requirements already cover this change.

relationships.when: A material technical choice remains after requirements are understood.
relationships.handoff: Requirements, observable acceptance checks, unchanged behavior and unresolved owner decisions. Once requirements are accepted, resolve any material technical choice; otherwise plan useful tasks or implement an already authorized bounded change.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: No material design choice remains; a missing architecture document alone is not a reason to add this step.

relationships.when: Accepted scope benefits from several independently verifiable tasks.
relationships.handoff: A justified design decision with alternatives, interfaces, failure modes, migration and rollback. Return requirement changes to their owner. Use accepted design for task planning only when breakdown helps, or for an already authorized bounded implementation.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: The authorized change is already one bounded task, or an accepted task plan remains current.

relationships.when: A bounded change and its edit/check authority are established.
relationships.handoff: Verifiable tasks with dependencies, consumed and produced interfaces, checks, allowed writes and unresolved holds. Select the next authorized bounded slice; planning alone starts neither implementation nor a goal.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: The requested scope is analysis only, or the actual slice is already implemented.

relationships.when: A real diff, commit or candidate needs judgment under the applicable review rules.
relationships.handoff: A focused patch, actual verification results and remaining limits for the authorized slice. Review the actual candidate as required. Keep subsequent repairs and hosted delivery within their existing authorization.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: The requested deliverable has no candidate, or valid review already covers the exact unchanged candidate; never waive a required review.

relationships.when: The accepted frame has material questions or lacks current G2 research evidence.
relationships.handoff: A solution-free frame, actual appetite, G0/G1 evidence and recorded human acceptance status. Begin Research only after current framing gates, engineering agreement and required answers are established. An explicit frame-only request stops at its accepted boundary.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: Current G2 evidence resolves the relevant stage questions; never invent research.

relationships.when: Accepted framing and current research support shaping within the actual appetite.
relationships.handoff: Source-backed findings that answer the stage questions, with coverage limits, unresolved uncertainties and current G2 evidence or hold. Shape a bounded solution only when current G2 prerequisites are met; material missing evidence remains in Research.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: A current shaped solution and all required diagrams/contracts are ready for review.

relationships.when: The current shaped packet needs the conductor review route, independent review and G3 evidence.
relationships.handoff: A bounded shaped candidate with required diagrams, interface and security contracts, risks and unresolved decisions. Carry the current packet to author audit and independent G3 review. Reopen Research or Framed when material uncertainty or scope changes require it.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: Valid G3 evidence covers the unchanged packet; a standalone pitch review does not fabricate workshop receipts.

relationships.when: Betting is in scope and approved targets or current G4 evidence remain incomplete.
relationships.handoff: Independent findings and repair dispositions tied to the shaped packet, with current G3 evidence or a review hold. Draft-only work stops at its accepted G3 boundary. Otherwise obtain actual team acceptance and complete approved target delivery before treating the package as ready for betting.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: Draft-only scope stops at its accepted boundary, or required targets and current G4 evidence are already verified.
relationships.to_stage: Verify authorized delivery and stage readiness

relationships.when: A bounded change and its edit/check authority are established.
relationships.handoff: Reproduction and discriminating evidence supporting a scoped cause or honest unknown, plus the proposed repair boundary. Implement a supported bounded repair when authorized; otherwise stop with the cause or missing observation. A passing retry alone proves neither cause nor fix.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: The requested scope is analysis only, or the actual slice is already implemented.

relationships.when: Actionable reviewer comments have been selected and their repair is authorized.
relationships.handoff: Actionable findings tied to the exact candidate, with reviewed coverage and limits. Apply selected actionable comments only when authorized, then re-review. If no repairs remain, assess the requested delivery gate without inferring merge or publication authority.
relationships.stop: Do not advance until the prior artifact/decision required for this step is actually accepted; preserve all unresolved holds. Skip if: No actionable selected comments need repair, or the request is review only.

relationships.when: An actual review contains selected actionable comments and repair is authorized.
relationships.handoff: Exact candidate identity, selected comment IDs, allowed repair scope and verification.
relationships.stop: No selected actionable feedback, missing edit authority or changed candidate.

relationships.when: A reviewed repair changes the candidate and needs re-review.
relationships.handoff: Fix commit/diff, addressed comment IDs and actual checks.
relationships.stop: Stop when required findings are resolved; do not loop on stylistic preference or repeat an unchanged failed approach.

relationships.when: Planning reveals an unresolved product acceptance decision that changes the intended outcome.
relationships.handoff: Specific ambiguity, affected requirement and decision owner; preserve accepted unaffected work.
relationships.stop: Do not restart the entire specification or invent the missing decision.

relationships.when: A material design choice contradicts accepted behavior and requires its owner to decide.
relationships.handoff: Concrete conflict, design alternatives and affected acceptance conditions.
relationships.stop: No authority to revise accepted scope; retain current contract until its owner decides.

relationships.when: Both read-only reviews are needed on one frozen candidate, neither consumes the other result, and the host authorizes the reviewer arrangement.
relationships.handoff: The same candidate hash, separate scopes and independent review outputs; combine findings after both finish.
relationships.stop: Candidate changes, output dependency, shared mutations, unavailable review support or absent host authority.

relationships.when: A long investigation now needs one recommendation from actual competing findings.
relationships.handoff: Attributed findings, alternatives, trade-offs and decision criteria.
relationships.stop: Missing alternatives or decision criteria remain questions, not fabricated inputs.

relationships.when: A requested faithful transcript is complete and the user also wants durable analysis.
relationships.handoff: Transcript identity, gaps, analysis goal and authorized scope.
relationships.stop: Do not mix new analysis into the faithful transcript.

relationships.when: A material capability instruction change is proposed for canonical admission.
relationships.handoff: Preservation/displacement record, exact candidate and existing owner.
relationships.stop: No silent canonical apply, installation or agent-surface expansion.

relationships.when: A claimed behavioral improvement needs bounded comparison rather than structural admission alone.
relationships.handoff: Baseline, candidate, task criteria and explicit experimental budget.
relationships.stop: Do not start a paid experiment without its required scope; structural readiness remains distinct.

relationships.when: An authorized repair produced a changed exact candidate and required findings need re-review.
relationships.handoff: Previous review, selected repair evidence and new candidate identity.
relationships.stop: Stop when required findings are resolved; unchanged candidates, no new evidence or exhausted agreed scope do not justify another pass.

relationships.when: The current shaping stage needs durable visual and contract evidence for a shaped solution.
relationships.handoff: Current accepted frame/research and supported solution seams; the helper retains component, sequence and data-flow diagrams plus full contracts and security ownership.
relationships.stop: Missing source support, unresolved upstream acceptance or required rendering evidence stays incomplete; do not invent internals or treat authoring as external placement.

source_refs.clause_ref: Full Shaping Handoff; Workflow; Required Output

relationships.when: The authored bundle passed completeness and the user requests a supported target representation or placement.
relationships.handoff: Exact source revision, complete diagram/table inventory, rendered observations and the actual target.
relationships.stop: Full-run placement waits for current G3 and actual publication authority; local conversion never proves external delivery.

relationships.when: Pitch review is part of a full shaping run, so the gate owner and its full rubric take precedence for that mode.
relationships.handoff: Actual pitch/evidence identities, current stage and independent non-author review context.
relationships.stop: Do not invent workshop history for a standalone pitch; absent historical evidence stays unassessed and required human decisions remain holds.

unmapped_relationship_policy: No curated edge is not a missing skill. Read its current full contract and establish a justified handoff.
